To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
delayed CTLA-Ig treatment is effective in reversing acute rejection, but does not eliminate memory T cells.
delayed CTLA-4 Ig treatment successfully rescues allospecific memory T cells from acute rejection and enables the acceptance of secondary allografts.
CTLA4Ig is able to inhibit established effector T cell-mediated acute kidney rejection in mice and to successfully rescue kidney transplant recipients from rejection in the clinic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunological basis of the efficacy of CTLA-4Ig-based immunotherapy in the clinic.
the development of new immunosuppressive strategies to prevent and treat acute rejection in solid organ transplantation.
the development of new therapies that will improve outcomes for patients undergoing organ transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CTLA4-I Ig is a very promising therapeutic agent that can successfully treat T cell-mediated acute allograft rejection in the mouse model, and that it is a very promising candidate for the treatment of acute rejection in humans.
the CTLA4-Igs can be used as an effective immunosuppressant to treat T cell mediated rejection, and the CTLA4-ig can inhibit the cytolytic activity, and IFNγ production by graft-infiltrated T cells.

CTLA4- Ig is able to partially inhibit the ongoing T-cell mediated acute rejection, but it does not reduce the numbers or the accumulation of antigen experienced donor-specific memory T-cells in the spleen, and this is the reason why the CTLA4-Iq-based immunosupression in clinic is successful to maintain long-term graft survival even after a T cell-mediated rejection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CTLA4Ig can control memory and effector T cells, and that CTLA4i can be used to treat acute rejection.
the efficacy of CTLA-4Ig therapy is not restricted to the early posttransplantation period, but can also be used in the setting of T cell-mediated acute allograft rejection.

CTLA4Ig therapy has the potential to treat and prevent rejection crises in patients receiving belatacept-based maintenance immunosuppression, and may be a valuable tool to treat acute rejection crises in patients who have received a T cell-depleting induction therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CTLA4Ig is able to control established T cell responses, even in the presence of memory T cells.

CTLA4-Immunoglobulin (CTLA4-Ig), which is a fusion protein between the extracellular domains of CTLA4 and the Fc portion of human immunoglobulin, is able to inhibit ongoing T cell-mediated rejection in the absence of B cells.
CTLA4-ig therapy can be used to treat T cell-mediated acute rejections in the clinic.
